title: Incomplete execution awaiting completion
problem: Stored incomplete executions may require manual completion or qualify for automatic retries.

likely_causes.cause: Completion depends on the error type and scenario settings.

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the error, storage and completion settings; review previous writes.

solutions.solution: Choose manual or automatic completion after checking retry eligibility and duplicate-write risk.
solutions.conditions: An incomplete execution is stored and its failure has been examined.

origin_details.evidence: ConnectionError and RateLimitError can be retried automatically without a Retry handler when incomplete-execution storage is enabled.

audit_notes: Documentary correction 2026-09-08; no verified real-case resolution.

title: Scenario operation timed out
problem: A Make module does not receive a response from an external service within Make's per-operation time limit. Make interrupts the execution. The timeout limit is enforced by Make's execution engine, but the root cause is typically the external service's response latency.
symptoms: Module shows a timeout-related error in execution history
Scenario stops at a specific HTTP or integration module
Error occurs consistently on large payloads or slow APIs
Error is intermittent on unstable external services

likely_causes.cause: External API is slow or overloaded and does not respond within Make's timeout window
Large file upload or download exceeds Make's response time window
Unstable network or DNS resolution failure on the external service
External service processes a heavy task synchronously instead of returning a quick response

diagnosis_steps: Open the failing execution and identify the exact module that timed out
Test the external API endpoint independently (Postman, curl) to measure its actual response time
Check the external service's status page for ongoing incidents
Reduce the payload size if the request involves file transfer or large JSON bodies and retest
Determine whether the error is consistent (service systematically too slow) or intermittent (flaky network or transient load)

solutions.solution: Add an Error Handler on the timing-out module with a Repeater configured for 3-5 retries with increasing delay intervals to automatically retry after transient timeouts
solutions.conditions: When the timeout is intermittent and the external service is normally responsive

solutions.solution: Split large requests into smaller batches using a Repeater or Iterator to reduce per-request processing time on the external service
solutions.conditions: When the timeout is caused by a large payload sent in a single request

solutions.solution: Adopt a webhook callback pattern: send the request asynchronously and configure the external service to call back a Make webhook when processing is complete
solutions.conditions: When the external service supports callbacks and processing inherently takes longer than Make's timeout allows

prevention: Attach an Error Handler with retry logic to HTTP modules calling slow external APIs
Prefer asynchronous webhook callback patterns for long-running external processes
Paginate or batch large requests instead of sending them in a single call

title: Monthly operations quota exhausted
problem: The Make account's monthly operations quota is fully consumed before the end of the billing period, causing all active scenarios to stop executing until the quota resets or is increased.
symptoms: Make dashboard shows operations counter at or near the plan maximum
Scenario executions show quota-related failure status

likely_causes.cause: A scenario with an Iterator or Repeater processing unexpectedly large volumes consumed operations at a high rate
A webhook trigger received a flood of events from an external system
A test or development scenario was left active in production mode
The plan's quota was underestimated for the actual sustained usage volume

diagnosis_steps: Go to Make Dashboard > Usage to see total operations consumption and the breakdown by scenario
Sort scenarios by operations consumed to identify the top consumers
Open the execution history of the top consumers and look for unexpected high-volume or runaway runs
Check whether a webhook trigger received an abnormal number of events recently
Look for active scenarios that were intended for testing only

solutions.solution: Pause all non-critical scenarios immediately to stop further operations consumption
solutions.conditions: Emergency response when quota is exhausted and critical scenarios must resume

solutions.solution: Upgrade the Make plan or purchase additional operations to restore execution capacity
solutions.conditions: When the volume is legitimate and the plan quota is insufficient

solutions.solution: Add filters on webhook triggers to reject irrelevant events before they trigger scenario execution
solutions.conditions: When a webhook event flood caused the exhaustion

solutions.solution: Reduce the frequency of scheduled scenarios or consolidate multiple scenarios into one to lower total operations count
solutions.conditions: When over-scheduling or redundant scenario architecture caused the exhaustion

prevention: Monitor operations usage regularly in the Make dashboard
Add filters on webhook triggers to reject irrelevant events
Deactivate test or development scenarios immediately after use

title: Scenario triggers itself — potential infinite loop
problem: A Make scenario, through its write actions, triggers its own execution again, creating a cycle. This rapidly exhausts the operations quota and may cause duplicate writes to external systems.
symptoms: Operations counter increases extremely rapidly in a short time window
Scenario execution history shows many identical executions within seconds
Make sends an operations quota warning very shortly after the scenario starts
External system shows repeated duplicate record writes

likely_causes.cause: The scenario triggered by a webhook writes to the same service that is the source of the webhook trigger, creating a feedback loop
Scenario A triggers Scenario B which triggers Scenario A — cross-scenario loop
A Watch trigger is on the same resource the scenario modifies — updating a record triggers the watch event again

diagnosis_steps: Check the execution history — if executions are happening at extremely high frequency within seconds, a cycle is very likely
Map the full trigger chain: identify what external event triggers the scenario, and what the scenario writes to
Determine whether the scenario's write actions could emit an event that re-triggers the scenario's trigger
Check for cross-scenario trigger chains that could form a cycle

solutions.solution: Add a dedicated field (e.g., 'make_processed') to the source system and set it during the scenario run. Add a filter at the start of the scenario to skip records where this flag is already set
solutions.conditions: When the source system supports custom fields and the field can be written by Make

solutions.solution: Use a Make Data Store to record IDs of processed records, and add a filter at the start of the scenario to skip already-processed IDs
solutions.conditions: When the source system cannot be modified with a custom field

solutions.solution: Change from an instant watch trigger to a scheduled polling trigger to reduce the feedback loop frequency
solutions.conditions: When instant triggering is not required and a processing delay is acceptable

prevention: Before deploying a scenario, explicitly map the full data flow and identify any write-to-trigger-source cycles
Use processed flags in source systems to prevent reprocessing of records already handled by Make
Monitor operations usage closely after deploying any new webhook-triggered scenario

origin_details.evidence: The infinite loop pattern is widely reported in Make community and is a logical consequence of Make's trigger architecture. No official documentation directly addresses cycle detection or prevention — this entry is based on community knowledge and technical inference. The Data Store solution is well-established. Source URL is the community root — no specific thread URL confirmed.
